title: Testing pure components
outcome: Explain testing pure components using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Test a room formatter alone. A pure function returns "Room " plus a supplied positive integer.
given: Accepted inputs are positive integers. Expected outputs: 7→"Room 7"; 12→"Room 12".

steps.label: Call with 7
steps.detail: The prefix and supplied numeral produce Room 7.

steps.label: Compare exact text
steps.detail: The expected text includes one space before 7.

steps.label: Call with 12
steps.detail: The same fixed procedure produces Room 12.

explanation: A pure component depends on its accepted input, not a clock, network or model. Isolating it makes failures easier to locate.

counterfactual.prediction: Reject the input under the stated positive-integer contract.
counterfactual.reason: Zero has the right type but violates the value requirement.

student_task: Predict the formatter outputs for 7 and 12, including spacing. Why does input 0 need rejection under this contract rather than an ordinary formatted response?
teacher_answer: The prefix and supplied numeral produce Room 7. The expected text includes one space before 7. The same fixed procedure produces Room 12. Changed case: Reject the input under the stated positive-integer contract. Zero has the right type but violates the value requirement.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: These tests cover only stated cases; they do not test the full AI service or every invalid value.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
